raw_response:
I am just going to tell you how I do it, like I have done for many years.

My 24 mu is split. I keep 18 mu for wheat and maize — one after the other, same land, every year. The other 6 mu I keep for cotton. Cotton does not like to come right after wheat on my land, and the picking time is different, so I keep it separate.

**For my wheat (18 mu, planted in October):**
I buy the compound fertilizer in the blue bag — the 15-15-15 one. One bag is 50 kg, and I put one bag on each mu when I plough. That is how everyone around here does it. Then in spring when the wheat stands up and starts to shoot, I spread urea — about half a bag per mu, maybe 25 kg. If the wheat looks yellow I add a little more, I would rather spend the money than see a thin crop. I water it two times usually — once before winter so the roots hold, and once in spring when it is heading. If the sky gives rain I skip one. For bugs and the rust disease I spray maybe twice — once for aphids, once when the ear comes out. I plough with the tractor before planting. Last year I got about 450 kg from each mu, I hope for the same.

**For my maize (18 mu, planted in June right after wheat):**
After wheat I do not plough again — too much work, and the wheat stubble is fine. I just plant right in with the seeder, no-till. I use the hybrid seed, the one the dealer in town sells, the kind my neighbor Wang uses because his maize is always tall. I put compound fertilizer in the row when I plant, about 40 kg per mu, and then when the maize is knee-high and making the big leaves I topdress urea, about 20 kg per mu. I water once or twice depending on rain — usually twice. I spray once for the borer worm. Maize gives me about 550 kg per mu.

**For my cotton (6 mu):**
Cotton is the one that costs me the most trouble. I plough deep before planting in April. I use the improved seed with the worm resistance, the Bt kind — without it the bollworm eats everything. I put one bag of compound per mu as base, and then I topdress urea two times, maybe 15 kg each time, once at budding and once at flowering. Cotton is hungry, it takes a lot. I water three or four times because cotton needs water when the bolls are filling. Pesticide I spray many times — five or six times — for aphids, spider mites, and the late worms. Cotton pays well if the bolls are clean, so I do not save on the spray. I hope for about 230 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I spend more on cotton inputs than on wheat and maize together, per mu. But cotton price is higher. My husband's nephew helps at picking time, I pay him in grain.
